stem:
With reference to Ocean Mean Temperature (OMT), which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. OMT is measured up to a depth of 26ºC isotherm which is 129 meters in the south-western Indian Ocean during January-March.
2. OMT collected during January-March can be used in assessing whether the amount of rainfall in monsoon will be less or more than a certain long-term mean.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
expl: The 26ºC isotherm is noticed at depths varying between 50- 100 meters. During January-March, the mean 26ºC isotherm in the south western Indian Ocean is at a depth of 59 meters. Ocean Mean Termperature (OMT) compared to sea surface temperature (SST) better predicts whether the total amount of rainfall that India will receive during monsoon season will be less or more than the long term mean of 887.5 mm.

stem: The surface of the earth covered with water is approximately?
expl: Around 29% (29.1%) of the total surface area of the Earth is land (about 148172000 sq. km) and 71% (70.9%) (about 361900000 sq. km) is covered by ocean. Hence, the surface of Earth covered with water is approximately more than two-thirds of the total surface area.

stem: A ridge of 64000 km. length and 2000 km to 2400 km width passing through the north and south Atlantic oceanic basin enter into the south pacific oceanic basin through Indian oceanic and then from the middle of Australia and Antarctic. This ridge is –
expl: Above qualities are related to Mid Oceanic Ridge. Mid Oceanic Ridge encircles the globe with a length of approximately 40390 miles or 65000 kilometer, covering the Arctic, Atlantic, Indian and Pacific Oceans. This is the single largest geological phenomenon on the surface of Earth.

Ninety East Ridge (90o E Ridge) is the name of a ridge located in the Indian Ocean. Located near 90o east longitude (meridian), this ridge is 5000 km long parallel to it and stretches from 34o south latitude to 10o north latitude with an average width of 200 km.

stem: The tension of gravitational water in the ground is –
expl: Gravitational water occupies the larger soil pores (macro-pores) and moves down readily under the force of gravity. Gravitational water under the surface of soil remains in a state of zero or less than 1/3 of the atmosphere.

Consider the following statements:
1. On the planet Earth, the fresh water available for use amounts to about less than 1% of the total water found.
2. Of the total freshwater found on the planet Earth, 95% is bound up in polar ice caps and glaciers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
expl: 96.5% of the total water available on Earth is salt water found in ocean. Out of the remaining 2.5% fresh water, 1.7% is in the form of glaciers and polar ice, which is unusable for us. So in this way total available fresh water to use is less than 1% of the total water available on Earth. Out of the total amount of fresh water (2.5%), 68.7% is found in the form of glaciers and polar ice, 30.1% in the form of underground water, 0.3% in the form of surface water and the remaining 0.9% is found in other forms. Hence only statement (1) is correct.

stem: Which one is the most extensive part of the oceanic floor?
expl: A most extensive part of the oceanic floor is 'Deep Sea Plain'. Characterized by flat and rolling submarine plain it is the most extensive relief zone of the ocean basins. These deep-sea plains (Abyssal Plains) having the depth of 3000 m to 6000 meter cover more than 76% percent of the total area of the ocean basins.

stem: Red sea is an example of :
expl: The Red Sea is an example of an axial trough, which lies between Africa and Arabia. A magnetic anomaly has been determined in this area. Countries with desert climates are located around the Red Sea due to high temperatures throughout the year. The cities of Jidd, Hejaz, Egypt, Suez and Aqaba etc. are situated on its banks. Due to the connection of North Africa and Europe with the countries of Asia through the Suez Canal, its commercial importance has increased significantly.

stem:
With reference to the Indian Ocean’, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It was called by the Ancient Greeks as Erythraean Sea.
2. It is spread on the either side of Equator.
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
Code :
expl: Statement 1 is correct. Ancient Greek geographers collectively referred to the vast sea waters of this region (including the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, Arabian Sea, and the northern Indian Ocean) as the “Erythraean Sea”; hence this name is seen in the context of the Indian Ocean. Statement 2 is correct. The Indian Ocean extends roughly from about 30° North latitude to 60° South latitude, and the Equator passes through it; therefore, it lies in both the Northern and Southern Hemispheres, i.e., on both sides of the Equator. Thus, both statements are correct, so the correct option is (c).
